samples.summary: Top-level design doc still asserts a GET→PUT losslessness invariant the new `lineHeight` band breaks
samples.evidence: rest-api.md:435-438 states "`GET` → edit → `PUT` stays lossless for docs bodies: the read side of the Tree codec (`@wafflebase/docs` `model/crdt-attrs.ts`) drops exactly the values the validator rejects." After this change that is no longer true for `lineHeight`: `parseBlockStyleAttrs` bands it to `(0, MAX_LINE_HEIGHT]`, while `assertValidBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:380) accepts any finite number — so a `PUT` of `1e9` or `0` is accepted and the following `GET` echoes `20` or the default. The new code comment in `crdt-attrs.ts` acknowledges the divergence explicitly, but the canonical REST design doc was not updated, leaving two documents disagreeing about the API contract. (Nested-doc/link checks do not cover this; the claim is prose, not a path.)
searchedFor: diff of docs/ hunks — no rest-api.md change present

samples.summary: New `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` ceiling on a user-draggable field is not recorded in the canonical `rowHeights` design doc
samples.evidence: docs-table-resize.md is the doc that defines `rowHeights` semantics and its constraint table ("| Row height | 20px (`MIN_ROW_HEIGHT`) | `max(userHeight, MIN_ROW_HEIGHT)` in layout |", line 248) plus the step-5b snippet the diff modifies (lines 200-210). This change adds an upper bound (`MAX_ROW_HEIGHT = 10000`) applied in that very step, so a drag past ~10 pages is now silently clamped, and adds step 5d substituting `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT` for non-finite heights. Both are recorded only in `docs.md` and the row-splitting doc, not where the field's constraints live, so the resize doc now understates the model rule.

samples.summary: HTML-paste producer of `fontSize` bypasses the band the design doc says the paste sanitizer applies
samples.evidence: The new docs.md text says "The paste sanitizer (`view/clipboard.ts`) is a *producer* of the same fields rather than a reader, and it calls the same bands: a value it admitted but a reader banded would leave the pasting client rendering something no peer, and no later reload, reproduces." That holds for the JSON path (`sanitizeInlineStyle` now calls `normalizeFontSize`), but `resolveInlineCSS` (clipboard.ts:547-553) — the external-HTML paste path in the same file — writes `style.fontSize` from CSS with no band at all, so pasting `font-size: 900000px` stores a value the CRDT readers clamp to `MAX_FONT_SIZE` on reload: exactly the local-vs-reload divergence the band was introduced to eliminate. The stated design is only half-applied within the module it names.

samples.summary: Substantial scope beyond the originating list-subtree issue: a five-attribute hardening program and a paginator bound ride along with #1050
samples.evidence: The issue the diff repeatedly cites is #1050 ("a parent never lands on the same level as its own child"), which `model/list-level.ts` plus the seven call sites satisfy on their own. Bundled with it are: a new `model/numeric-attrs.ts` banding `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`padding`/image size, `model/row-height.ts`, `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` in `pagination.ts`, `computeTableLayout` step 5d, clipboard sanitizer changes, the `crdt-attrs.ts` `lineHeight` band, `YorkieDocStore` changes and a frontend constant rewire — a separate DoS/robustness concern with its own design-doc sections. Only `normalizeListLevel` is actually needed by the list fix. This is reviewable-scope creep rather than a behavioral defect; a reviewer cannot weigh the list-hierarchy change independently of the hardening. (No issue text was supplied to me, so this is graded on the #1050 references in the diff itself.)

samples.summary: `walkCellsForSiblings` re-implements `walkCellsForBlock`'s traversal instead of sharing one walk
samples.evidence: `walkCellsForBlock` (document.ts:~78) and the new `walkCellsForSiblings` (document.ts:91-112) recurse over the identical rows→cells→nested-blocks structure and differ only in what they return (the block vs. its containing array). One walk returning `{ block, siblings }`, or `walkCellsForBlock` returning the container, would avoid two copies of the nesting logic that must now be kept in step.

samples.summary: `model/list-level.ts` mixes a model-level numeric band with an editor gesture planner
samples.evidence: The module holds both `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`/`normalizeListLevel` (a model invariant every reader — layout, PDF, markdown, PPTX — imports) and `planListLevelChanges`/`subtreeOf`/`planSiblingGroup` (an editing-command planner used only by the two editors). The sibling bands (`row-height.ts`, `numeric-attrs.ts`) are pure bands, and the header of `numeric-attrs.ts` even justifies the split by "a gesture plans with them" — which inverts the usual layering, since the gesture layer could import the band rather than the band module hosting the gesture. No behavioral consequence.
